name: Debug like a Human: A Large Language Model Debugger via Verifying Runtime Execution Step by Step
authors: Li (Lily) Zhong, Zilong Wang, Jingbo Shang; University of California, San Diego (UC San Diego)
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024 (pages 851-870)
reflection_type: tool-verified (verbal self-critique grounded in runtime execution traces): the LLM verbally verifies each basic block, but its critique is anchored to actual runtime variable values collected by an instrumented interpreter and to pass/fail signals from visible test cases
feedback_source: external-tool (program interpreter producing runtime execution traces / intermediate variable values) combined with unit-tests (visible test cases that determine pass/fail and drive the execution); the LLM itself acts as the block-level judge over this collected runtime evidence
iteration_structure: iterative-refine: a three-step loop (collect runtime info on the failed visible test -> block-by-block correctness verification -> detect buggy block and regenerate) repeated until the new program passes all visible tests or a maximum debugging iteration is reached (no episode reset; the program is repaired in place)
reflection_object: output content (the generated program / code) and its execution behavior. LDB does not modify weights, prompts-as-skills, or a persistent memory; it reflects on the program's runtime execution flow segmented into basic blocks (control-flow units with their intermediate variable values) and rewrites the buggy program.
requires_training: none (training-free; works with frozen LLM backbones such as GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4-1106-preview, CodeLlama-34B, StarCoder-15B via prompting only)
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge grounded by verifiable signal: the same LLM serves as the block-level verifier/critic, but correctness is ultimately gated by a verifiable reward (visible unit-test pass/fail) plus deterministic runtime variable values; there is no separately trained reward or critic model
distillation_target: none (no reusable artifact is distilled; each task's debugging is ephemeral and confined to repairing that single program. No episodic memory, skill library, or learned prompt is persisted across tasks.)
emergent_vs_engineered: prompt/scaffold-engineered: the reflective debugging behavior is an explicitly engineered pipeline (control-flow-graph segmentation into basic blocks, interpreter instrumentation to capture intermediate variable values, batched block-verification prompts, regeneration). It is not an RL-emergent reflection capability.
memory_type: short-term/scratchpad: within a debugging episode the LLM is given the runtime execution information (blocks + intermediate variable values) and prior debugging messages for the current program; no long-term or cross-task memory store
memory_persistence: within-episode (the runtime trace and debugging dialogue are scoped to repairing one program for one task; nothing persists across tasks or sessions)
memory_curation_mechanism: retrieval-gated / selective sampling: when an execution trace is too long to fit the LLM token limit, LDB selectively samples N_b basic blocks from the trace and batches the intermediate states into a single query (batch debugging) to stay within the context window; otherwise the per-episode context is append-style debugging messages
error_localization_granularity: block-level (code): programs are segmented via the control-flow graph into basic blocks, intermediate variable values are tracked at the end of each block, and the LLM gives a per-block correctness verdict to pinpoint the buggy block. An ablation shows block-level outperforms both line-level (incomplete semantics per unit) and function-level (too coarse, ~8.1 iterations on average, highest token cost).
intra_task_vs_inter_task: intra-task: LDB refines a single program within one task using that task's visible test cases and runtime trace; it does not transfer learned experience across tasks
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: post-hoc-revision: a failing seed program is detected (fails a visible test), localized to a buggy block, and regenerated/repaired after the fact; it iterates on the same task rather than retrying a fresh episode or correcting mid-generation
task_domains: code (program synthesis / code generation and code translation / debugging)
benchmarks: HumanEval, MBPP, TransCoder (text-to-code for HumanEval/MBPP and C++-to-Python translation for TransCoder); also used to debug seed programs from GPT-4 and Reflexion on HumanEval
headline_result: LDB consistently improves Pass@1 by up to +9.8% across HumanEval, MBPP, and TransCoder over multiple frozen LLM backbones; e.g. with GPT-3.5 on HumanEval 73.8 -> 82.9 (+9.1); the largest single gain is CodeLlama-34B on TransCoder 69.8 -> 79.6 (+9.8). Debugging Reflexion seed programs with a GPT-3.5 backbone reaches 95.1% on HumanEval, a new SOTA at the time.
baselines: Baseline w/o debugger (seed programs); Self-Debugging (Chen et al. 2023) in two variants: Self-Debugging (+Expl.) prompting line-by-line explanation, and Self-Debugging (+Trace) prompting the LLM to dry-run the program. LDB vs Self-Debugging is the head-to-head comparison.
gains_vs_baseline: Vs the strongest Self-Debugging variant, LDB is higher and more stable. GPT-3.5: HumanEval 82.9 vs SD 81.1 (+1.8), TransCoder 87.7 vs 86.1 (+1.6), MBPP 76.0 vs 74.4 (+1.6). CodeLlama-34B TransCoder 79.6 vs 79.4. StarCoder-15B HumanEval +0.6 where SD (+Expl.) degrades to -0.6, showing LDB avoids the harmful self-correction Self-Debugging can cause. On advanced generators (GPT-3.5 backbone): GPT-4 seeds 75.0 -> 82.9 (LDB +7.9 vs SD +7.3); Reflexion seeds 91.5 -> 95.1 (LDB +3.6 vs SD +0.6).
compute_cost_profile: Inference-only multiplier (no training cost). Each debugging iteration adds interpreter instrumentation plus multiple LLM calls (block verification + regeneration); batch debugging amortizes verification into a single query to reduce token cost. Block-level decomposition is the cheapest effective setting: line-level and especially function-level cost more tokens (function-level needs ~8.1 iterations on average). Total cost is bounded by the maximum debugging iteration; exact API-call multiplier vs single-pass not reported as a single figure.
known_limitations: Correct visible test cases are mandatory: LDB needs at least one correct test to execute the program and compare the runtime flow against the task description. It explicitly leaves test-case-free debugging (self-correcting purely from intermediate execution without knowing whether the result is correct) as an open question. It is also bounded by the limitations of human-style debugging methods and by LLM context limits on long traces (mitigated by block sampling).
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: external-tool/verifier plus oracle-style test signal: relies on a program interpreter (runtime traces / intermediate variables) AND on visible unit test cases that act as the correctness oracle to trigger and terminate debugging. It is NOT intrinsic-only self-correction; the gains depend on this external verifiable feedback, consistent with the Huang/Kamoi critique that intrinsic self-correction without external signal is unreliable.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive but external-feedback-dependent: with visible test cases and runtime traces, LDB delivers consistent gains across backbones and even repairs strong generators (GPT-4, Reflexion). The StarCoder result is illustrative: Self-Debugging (+Expl.) degrades the baseline (-0.6) on HumanEval whereas LDB stays positive (+0.6), showing the grounded block-level verification mitigates the harmful self-correction that pure verbal self-debugging can cause; efficacy still requires the test-case oracle (not label-free).
calibration_effect: not-measured (the paper does not study confidence calibration or a reasoning-tax effect; it targets code-generation accuracy on classical LLMs, not o1/R1-style reasoning models)
failure_attribution_capability: attributes-failing-step: within a single program LDB performs counterfactual/step-style localization by issuing per-basic-block correctness verdicts against the task description to identify which block is buggy. It does not classify a taxonomy of failure modes nor attribute responsibility across multiple agents (single-agent code repair).
failure_mode_addressed: Targets logic/implementation bugs in LLM-generated code, especially programs with complex control flow and data operations where treating the program as an indivisible whole fails. By grounding verification in runtime variable values it counters superficial self-reflection / hallucinated reasoning about code behavior (an LLM dry-run can mis-simulate execution); not framed against MAST's multi-agent failure taxonomy.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new benchmark dataset is released; code and the experimental dataset/setup are released at https://github.com/FloridSleeves/LLMDebugger (uses existing HumanEval, MBPP, TransCoder).
builds_on: Self-Debugging / Teaching LLMs to Self-Debug (Chen et al. 2023, the primary baseline and rubber-duck-debugging predecessor); Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023, verbal self-reflection with test feedback, used as a seed-program generator); Self-Refine (Madaan et al. 2023, iterative self-feedback); classical compiler theory (control-flow graphs / basic blocks, Allen 1970; Aho-Ullman). It extends test-driven iterative refinement by adding runtime execution / intermediate-variable evidence at block granularity.
extended_by_or_inspired: Successor fine-grained code-debugging work, e.g. MGDebugger / 'Closing the Last Mile of Code Generation with Hierarchical Debugging' (hierarchical multi-granularity debugging), 'Execution Guided Line-by-Line Code Generation', 'ReCode: Improving LLM-based Code Repair with Fine-Grained Retrieval-Augmented Generation', and 'Static Analysis as a Feedback Loop: Enhancing LLM-Generated Code Beyond Correctness'; also cited by surveys of self-correction and execution-feedback-based code generation.
citation_count: 171 (Semantic Scholar, as of 2026-06; corpus id 268032812, DOI 10.18653/v1/2024.findings-acl.49)
on_policy_distillation_link: Not applicable / no link: LDB is a training-free inference-time debugging loop and distills nothing into weights or a reusable policy, so it has no relation to on-policy distillation or skill-optimization; any improvement is per-task and ephemeral.
sample_efficiency: Bounded by a maximum debugging iteration per program. Reported iteration statistics by decomposition level: function-level needs ~8.1 iterations on average (most expensive), while block-level (the default) reaches its gains with substantially fewer iterations/tokens; an exact average iteration count for the block-level default is not stated in the fetched text.
